Some Technical Techniques in the Swahili Novel: "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman as an Example
Jalgham Abuazuom Emhemmed Ali
Department of African Languages and Studies, Faculty of Languages, Sebha University, Libya
Keywords: Novel, Written Literature, Technical Techniques, Style, Literature

A B S T R A C T
A work of literature, including a novel, is formed by technique and content, which together constitute what we refer to as literature. Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and the use of language. These elements are utilized by writers in various ways depending on their skills and abilities. In terms of technique, it refers to the overall main ideas expressed by the author or narrator of the literary work and intended for the audience to receive. This work was intended to investigate the various themes presented by Mohamed Suleiman in his Swahili novel "Kiu." Through this novel, we have identified and discussed the literary techniques used by the author to bring out the themes within the novel. 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. While Bahati is deeply immersed in love, unaware of herself and her surroundings, she realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but instead loves only himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely an instrument to fulfill his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a snare, her efforts to find escape only lead her closer to ruin. Introduction

3. The Swahili novel is one of the four genres of written Swahili literature, the others being drama, poetry, and the short story (Wamitila, 2008). The novel genre is used to explain matters in greater depth and breadth than other genres of written literature. As a result, the novel conveys political, social, and cultural themes to society through the stories and events presented in the specific novel. Mohamed Suleiman is one of the authors of Swahili novels who crafts various stories and events that present substantial themes for society. 4. The novel 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. Lost in love and oblivious to herself, Bahati realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but rather loves himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely a tool for fulfilling his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a trap, her efforts to find escape only bring her ruin. The novel 'Kiu' won first prize in the Kiswahili fiction writing competition, which was organized in 1970. 5. What is technique? Technique is the artistic craftsmanship employed by a writer when composing or narrating their literary work before the specific audience intended for that work. Technique encompasses elements such as use of language, structure, style, characters, and setting. Together, these elements enable the writer of a literary work to construct and convey their themes and ideas to the intended audience. The use of these technical elements varies, and may sometimes even be similar, from one writer to another. Mohamed Suleiman, in the novel 'Kiu', has employed various literary techniques to present the themes to the intended audience; however, in this work, we cannot address all of the techniques. Some of the artistic techniques we have examined in this work include the use of letters, suspense, proverbs, metaphors, and personification. 5.1.1 The Use of the Letter Technique  
A letter is an ancient means of communication between an individual and another individual, an individual and a group, an institution and an individual, or between institutions. Its aim is to convey information or a particular message that is important for the intended recipient to know.  
Idi received the letter with surprise because he was not expecting it. He turned the letter over and saw Bahati’s name written in hurried handwriting. He opened it and read:  
Idi,  
Don’t be surprised when I tell you that right now I am in bed with Mr. Mwinyi, and we are planning the day for our real wedding. It is not permitted to interfere with us because we have our own free will. I warn you for your own safety, that your plans should cease once you have received this letter. Send my regards to so-and-so … From the depths of my heart, Bahati. The letter ignited a fire in Idi’s heart and boiled him with anger. It struck him like a sudden, fierce storm. Suddenly his eyes changed color, his forehead became furrowed, and his jaw dropped, in a display of intense anguish. He read that letter again, and the more he read it, the angrier he became. 58-59). This letter was written by Bahati to Idi, her lover whom she loves very much, but here she is informing him that she is now in love with another person named Mwinyi. Mwinyi is Idi's boss, and Idi wanted Bahati to deceive Mwinyi by making him believe she loved him so that they could get money, while in reality, the one she truly loved was Idi. Now, it is truly shocking to see that the love between Mwinyi and Bahati has become genuine and not a joke as Idi had expected. Idi is now filled with great doubt about whether the wealth he hoped to gain from Mwinyi through Bahati will actually materialize, or if it has already been lost. The theme of love, as well as that of theft and smuggling, are greatly developed through the use of the letter mentioned above. Bahati is weighing whether Idi truly loves her, while Idi grows angry as his plan to gain Mwinyi's wealth through Bahati slips away. Also, through the above letter, the author develops the theme that not everything can turn out as one expects. Planning and implementation of something are two different things, although they are interdependent (Scott, 1995). Idi did not expect that telling Bahati to pretend to love Mwinyi so they could gain wealth would actually make Bahati truly fall in love with Mwinyi and leave him. Here, the theme of warnings is developed, emphasizing that love should not be experimented with, as at any moment it can change and become completely different from what was originally intended. Proverbs are expressions that are similar to and resemble sayings used by human beings as tools of communication (Msokile, 1992). However, proverbs often do not have two sides as is the case with sayings. A proverb, on its part, has two sides, where one side serves as a question and the other side provides the answer to the question posed (Wamitila, 2003). Proverbs are sayings that arise from expressions whose nature is that they emerge and disappear, and those that do not disappear but endure are what are called proverbs. Proverbs are a literary technique used by authors of literary works to underscore or emphasize a particular theme they want their audience to grasp. In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her. Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately. The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child. Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008). If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged. 5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences. For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all. The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader. Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing. That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01). The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value. Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him. Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand. This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person. Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011). However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything. This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love. Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi. He says:
There was a brief but bitter silence. Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing. Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you. I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart. He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him. Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come. But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02). The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something. “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked. Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006). Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape. The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison. For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison. 5.1.4 The Use of Personification

However, it is said that the issue was actually a person’s temperament—and that person is arrogant and boastful. These descriptions show that the thing in question is not specified, which makes the keen reader want to find out what exactly it is that is troubling Mwinyi so much. The use of suspense will compel the reader to continue reading the novel 'Kiu' until they discover what it is that is bothering Mwinyi. As the reader continues, they come across the following words:  
Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989). Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006). The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them. In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed. She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken. Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20). The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human. 5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience. This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006). The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader. Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst. If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had. But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride. So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02). This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy. This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him. “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five. This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth. That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school. In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati. The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu. This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991). For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter. After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father. Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety. Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety. The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research. The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati. Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him. It turned out that Iddi was not upset because he really loved Bahati; rather, he saw clearly Some Stylistic Techniques in Swahili Novels: "The Novel Kiu by Mohamed Suleiman as an Example" Ali. Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream. Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense. The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person. The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman. Other stylistic techniques used to develop social themes in the novel "Kiu" include proverbs, metaphors, and personification. A B S T R A C T
Kazi ya fasihi, pamoja na riwaya, huundwa na mbinu na maudhui, ambayo kwa pamoja huunda kile tunachorejelea kuwa fasihi. Mbinu huundwa na vipengele kama vile wahusika, mtindo, mpangilio, muundo na matumizi ya lugha. Vipengele hivi vinatumiwa na waandishi kwa njia mbalimbali kulingana na ujuzi na uwezo wao. Kwa upande wa mbinu, inarejelea mawazo makuu ya jumla yanayotolewa na mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi ya fasihi na yanayokusudiwa hadhira kupokea. Kazi hii ilikusudiwa kuchunguza dhamira mbalimbali zilizowasilishwa na Mohamed Suleiman katika riwaya yake ya Kiswahili "Kiu." Kupitia riwaya hii, tumebainisha na kujadili mbinu za kifasihi alizotumia mwandishi kuleta dhamira ndani ya riwaya. Idi haraka anamnasa Bahati katika mtego wa mapenzi ya uongo. Bahati akiwa amezama sana katika mapenzi, hajitambui na mazingira yake, anagundua kuwa Idi hampendi kikweli, badala yake anajipenda yeye tu, na yeye Bahati ni chombo tu cha kutimiza matamanio yake ya kidunia. Utanzu wa riwaya hutumika kueleza mambo kwa kina na mapana zaidi kuliko tanzu nyinginezo za fasihi andishi. Kutokana na hali hiyo, riwaya inawasilisha dhamira za kisiasa, kijamii na kitamaduni kwa jamii kupitia hadithi na matukio yanayowasilishwa katika riwaya mahususi. Mohamed Suleiman ni mmoja wa watunzi wa riwaya za Kiswahili wanaotunga hadithi na matukio mbalimbali yanayowasilisha dhamira muhimu kwa jamii. 4. Riwaya ya 'Kiu' ni riwaya ya Kiswahili inayosimulia kisa cha Bahati, msichana aliyelelewa kwa uangalifu na sasa anakutana na Idi, mwanamume tapeli. Idi haraka anamnasa Bahati katika mtego wa mapenzi ya uongo. Akiwa amepoteza upendo na kujisahau, Bahati anatambua kwamba Idi hampendi kikweli, bali anajipenda mwenyewe, na kwamba yeye, Bahati, ni chombo tu cha kutimiza matamanio yake ya kidunia. Kama ndege aliyenaswa kwenye mtego, jitihada zake za kutafuta njia ya kutoroka zinamletea uharibifu. Riwaya ya 'Kiu' ilishinda tuzo ya kwanza katika shindano la uandishi wa hadithi za Kiswahili, ambalo liliandaliwa mnamo 1970. 5. Mbinu ni nini? Mbinu ni ufundi wa kisanaa unaotumiwa na mwandishi wakati wa kutunga au kusimulia kazi yao ya kifasihi mbele ya hadhira mahususi iliyokusudiwa kwa kazi hiyo. Mbinu hujumuisha vipengele kama vile matumizi ya lugha, muundo, mtindo, wahusika na mpangilio. Kwa pamoja vipengele hivi vinamwezesha mwandishi wa kazi ya fasihi kujenga na kufikisha dhamira na mawazo yake kwa hadhira iliyokusudiwa. Matumizi ya vipengele hivi vya kiufundi hutofautiana, na wakati mwingine inaweza kuwa sawa, kutoka kwa mwandishi mmoja hadi mwingine. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya ya 'Kiu', ametumia mbinu mbalimbali za kifasihi kuwasilisha dhamira kwa walengwa; hata hivyo, katika kazi hii, hatuwezi kushughulikia mbinu zote. Baadhi ya mbinu za kisanaa tulizozichunguza katika kazi hii ni pamoja na matumizi ya herufi, mashaka, methali, tamathali za semi na tashihisi. Mbinu inarejelea ufundi wa kisanaa unaotumiwa na mwandishi kutengeneza kazi zao ili wasomaji na wasikilizaji waweze kuifurahia (Njogu na Chimerah, 1999). Mbinu huundwa na vipengele kama vile wahusika, mtindo, mpangilio, muundo na matumizi ya lugha. Vipengele hivi hutumiwa na waandishi kwa njia tofauti kulingana na ujuzi na ujuzi wao. (SI kitendawili, 2011). 5.1 Mbinu za Kifasihi katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili  
5.1.1 Matumizi ya Mbinu ya Barua  
Barua ni njia ya kale ya mawasiliano kati ya mtu binafsi na mtu mwingine, mtu binafsi na kikundi, taasisi na mtu binafsi, au kati ya taasisi. Lengo lake ni kuwasilisha taarifa au ujumbe fulani ambao ni muhimu kwa mlengwa kuufahamu.  
Idi aliipokea barua hiyo kwa mshangao kwa sababu hakuitarajia. Aligeuza barua na kuona jina la Bahati limeandikwa kwa mwandiko wa haraka haraka. Akaifungua na kusoma:  
Idi,  
Usishangae ninapokuambia kuwa sasa hivi niko kitandani kwa Mheshimiwa Mwinyi, na tunapanga siku ya harusi yetu halisi. Hairuhusiwi kutuingilia kwa sababu tuna hiari yetu wenyewe. Ninakuonya kwa usalama wako mwenyewe, kwamba mipango yako inapaswa kukoma mara tu utakapopokea barua hii. Tuma salamu zangu kwa fulani ... Kutoka ndani ya moyo wangu, Bahati. Barua hiyo iliwasha moto moyoni mwa Idi na kumchemsha kwa hasira. Ilimpata kama dhoruba kali ya ghafla. Ghafla macho yake yakabadilika rangi, paji la uso likawa na mifereji, na taya yake ikaanguka, kwa maonyesho ya uchungu mkali. Aliisoma tena barua hiyo, na kadiri alivyozidi kuisoma, ndivyo alivyozidi kuwa na hasira. 58-59). Barua hii iliandikwa na Bahati kwenda kwa Idi, mpenzi wake ambaye anampenda sana, lakini hapa anamtaarifu kuwa sasa yuko kwenye mapenzi na mtu mwingine anayeitwa Mwinyi. Mwinyi ni bosi wa Idi, na Idi alimtaka Bahati amdanganye Mwinyi kwa kumfanya aamini kuwa anampenda ili wapate pesa, kumbe kiukweli aliyempenda kwa dhati ni Idi. Sasa inashangaza sana kuona mapenzi kati ya Mwinyi na Bahati yamekuwa ya kweli na si mzaha kama Idi alivyotarajia. Idi sasa ameingiwa na mashaka makubwa iwapo utajiri aliotarajia kuupata kutoka kwa Mwinyi kupitia kwa Bahati utatimia kweli, au tayari umeshapotea. Mandhari ya mapenzi, pamoja na ile ya wizi na magendo, yanaendelezwa sana kwa kutumia barua iliyotajwa hapo juu. Bahati anapima iwapo Idi anampenda kweli, huku Idi akipandwa na hasira huku mpango wake wa kupata utajiri wa Mwinyi kupitia Bahati ukiporomoka. Pia, kupitia barua hiyo hapo juu, mwandishi huendeleza mada ambayo sio kila kitu kinaweza kutokea kama mtu anatarajia. Kupanga na kutekeleza jambo ni vitu viwili tofauti, ingawa vinategemeana (Scott, 1995). Idi hakutarajia kuwa kumwambia Bahati ajifanye anampenda Mwinyi ili wapate mali kwa kweli kungemfanya Bahati kumpenda sana Mwinyi na kumuacha. Hapa, mada ya maonyo inakuzwa, ikisisitiza kwamba upendo haupaswi kujaribiwa, kwani wakati wowote unaweza kubadilika na kuwa tofauti kabisa na kile kilichokusudiwa hapo awali. Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kisanaa katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili: 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano - Ali. 5.1.2 Matumizi ya Methali katika Kiu

Methali ni semi zinazofanana na kufanana na semi zinazotumiwa na binadamu kama nyenzo za mawasiliano (Msokile, 1992). Walakini, methali mara nyingi hazina pande mbili kama ilivyo kwa misemo. Methali kwa upande wake ina pande mbili, ambapo upande mmoja hutumika kama swali na upande mwingine hutoa jibu la swali lililoulizwa (Wamitila, 2003). Methali ni misemo itokanayo na misemo ambayo asili yake ni kuibuka na kutoweka, na ile isiyotoweka bali huvumilia ndiyo inayoitwa methali. Methali ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi ili kusisitiza au kusisitiza dhamira fulani wanayotaka hadhira yao ielewe. Katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman ametumia methali katika kazi yake kama ifuatavyo: Mambo hayakuwa mazuri kwa Idi, kwani nia yake haikuwa kumpenda kikweli bali kumchezea tu. Wazazi wengi wanaowajibika wanajua kuwa vijana wanapoingia kwenye mahusiano ya kimapenzi kabla ya ndoa mara nyingi huwapelekea kuchezeana na suala la ndoa kupotea. Kwa hiyo, akiwa mzazi, Cheusi alimtaka bintiye kumalizana na Idi mara moja. Methali iliyotumika katika kifungu hapo juu imetumika kujenga na kusisitiza mada ya mwongozo wa mama kwa mtoto wake. Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mazoea ni kitu ambacho hutengeneza tabia, na mazoea daima yanaendelea (Ritzer, 2008). Iwapo katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wataachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa, wataichukulia kuwa inakubalika, na suala la kuoana halitakuwa na umuhimu wowote kwao. Wazazi watimize wajibu wao ipasavyo ili wanajamii hasa vijana waone kuwa mahusiano kabla ya ndoa ni jambo baya ambalo halipaswi kuhimizwa kamwe. 5.1.3 Matumizi ya Sitiari katika Kiu

Tamathali ya semi ni tamathali ya semi ambayo hutumiwa kulinganisha vitu viwili vyenye sifa tofauti bila kutumia viunganishi vya ulinganishi, kama ilivyo kwa tashibiha (Kyando, 2013). Vitu vinavyolinganishwa vinachukuliwa kuwa sawa kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote. Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza kusema, "Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo aliyejificha kwenye mti." Hapa Mwajuma anafananishwa na sungura kana kwamba ni vitu viwili vinavyofanana kabisa bila tofauti yoyote. Madhumuni makuu ya kutumia mafumbo katika kazi za fasihi ni kusisitiza dhamira inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji. Mohamed Suleiman alitumia sitiari aliposema:  
Watu waliposema hakuna aliyewahi kumzidi ujanja Mwinyi, maneno yao hayakuwa ya kutia chumvi. Mwinyi alikuwa na pesa za kutosha kujinunulia vitu vingi ambavyo mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angeweza kutamani, isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu. Hilo ndilo lililomfanya ahisi kana kwamba maisha yake yote yamepotea, na kwamba utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki ya wali iliyoharibiwa na mchanga (uk.01). Maneno yaliyosisitizwa kwa wino katika msemo hapa yanaeleza msemo kwamba kitu kizuri sasa kimegeuka kuwa kibaya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu, na kitu cha thamani sasa kimepoteza thamani yake. Bwana Mwinyi alikuwa ni tajiri mwenye kila aina ya utajiri, lakini alitamani sana kuwa na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na mwanadada Bahati ambaye alikuwa akimpenda sana. Kila mbinu aliyoijaribu ilishindikana kumshinda Bahati, hali iliyopelekea kulalamika kuwa “utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki iliyochanganywa na mchanga,” akimaanisha utajiri wake haukumsaidia chochote na wala haukuwa na faida yoyote kwake. Kimsingi, keki ya wali iliyochanganywa na mchanga huwa haiwezi kuliwa na kupoteza ladha yake yote kwa sababu mlaji anaogopa meno yake yatauma kwenye mchanga. Msemo huu kwa hakika umetumika kutilia mkazo mada ya mapenzi—kwamba ikiwa mtu ni tajiri katika kila maana ya kimaada lakini akakosa upendo anaoutamani, basi utajiri wake unakuwa hauna maana na kuwafanya waishi kwa dhiki na uchungu wa akili kuliko hata maskini. Wanasosholojia wanakiri kwamba kuna vitu fulani ambavyo kwa ujumla huchukuliwa kuwa vya kutamanika sana kuwa navyo, kama vile utajiri (Cross, 2011). Hata hivyo, inafika wakati mtu anakosa kitu ambacho alidhani ni kidogo, na mali yake haimsaidii kukipata, ingawa aliamini kuwa utajiri wake ndio ufunguo wa kupata kila kitu. Hii ni sawa na kusema kwamba keki ya wali sasa ina mchanga ndani yake, kwa kuwa utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haungeweza kumwezesha kushinda penzi la Bahati. Matumizi mengine ya msemo huo yanaonekana wakati Cheusi, ambaye ni mamake Bahati, alipokuwa akimwonya bintiye kuhusu uhusiano wake na Idi. Anasema:
Kukawa kimya kifupi lakini kichungu. Kisha Cheusi akaendelea kumshauri: “Huyo Idi wako hebu niambie hakutaki hana lolote. Yeyote anayetamani mwanamke kweli amuoe. Anataka tu kukuchezea kisha akutupe, akiendelea huku anakucheka. Tayari nimegundua kwamba kwa sababu tu umesoma Kiingereza chako unafikiri mimi sijui, basi ... Siku moja utalia kama mbwa, utainua mdomo, na nitakuwa hapa (uk. 25–26).” Katika kifungu hiki mwandishi anatumia msemo, “utalia kama mbwa, mdomo utainuliwa,” kurejelea mada ya mwongozo na maonyo yanayotolewa na mama kwa mtoto wake. Cheusi alikuwa akimwonya bintiye Bahati kuhusu uhusiano aliokuwa ameanza nao
Muda huo Iddi dereva wake aliingia bila kubisha hodi. Mwinyi alishtuka na kumuuliza, “Mbona umechelewa?” Iddi alijifuta jasho kuonesha juhudi aliyoifanya, akatikisa kichwa kwa huzuni na kusema, “Nimekuta mlango umefungwa.” Maneno hayo yalivunja moyo wa Mwinyi. Aliinama mabega yake na kujikunyata kwenye kiti, akihisi maisha hayakuwa ya haki kwake. Kungoja bila mwisho—miezi sita ilikuwa imepita, na hamu isiyokoma ililemea sana. Alikuwa tayari amevumilia vya kutosha; lakini bado hakujua siku ya msaada ingefika lini. Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: "Chochote kinachokuja kwa njia yako, kikubali" (uk. 02). Matumizi ya sitiari katika kishazi hapo juu yanaonyesha kuwa maneno hulinganishwa na kisu au kitu chochote chenye ncha kali chenye uwezo wa kukata kitu. "Maneno yale yalimpiga Mwinyi sana," ni kauli inayoonyesha matumaini ya Mwinyi kumshinda Bahati yalitoweka mara tu alipopata taarifa kutoka kwa Idi kwamba hakumpata Bahati na kwamba mlango wa Bahati ulikuwa umefungwa. Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kwamba mtu anaweza kufikia mahali ambapo anapoteza matumaini ya kupata kitu ambacho amekuwa akitamani kwa muda mrefu lakini hawezi kukipata (Webster, 2006). Kupoteza tumaini maishani ni jambo baya kwa sababu kunaweza kumfanya mtu afanye jambo baya ambalo linaweza hata kuhatarisha wengine. Kwa mfano, kukata tamaa kwa Mwinyi kwa kukosa kuwa na Bahati kunaweza kumfanya achukue uamuzi wa kufanya uhalifu kama vile ubakaji. Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya kwa mwathiriwa lakini pia kwa mhusika, kwani kinaweza kusababisha kukaa jela maisha yake yote. Kwa mzee wa miaka sitini na mbili kama Mwinyi kufungwa ni jambo baya sana ambalo linaweza kumfanya afie gerezani. 5.1.4 Matumizi ya Utu  
JOHS Vol.22 No. Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kifasihi katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiswahili 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" Ali. pesa zote kutoka kwa utajiri wake. Hata hivyo, inasemekana kwamba suala hilo kwa kweli lilikuwa tabia ya mtu—na mtu huyo ni mwenye kiburi na majivuno. Maelezo haya yanaonesha kuwa jambo husika halijaainishwa, jambo linalomfanya msomaji makini kutaka kujua ni nini hasa kinachomsumbua sana Mwinyi. Matumizi ya mashaka yatamlazimisha msomaji kuendelea kusoma riwaya ya 'Kiu' hadi agundue ni kitu gani kinamsumbua Mwinyi. Wakati msomaji anaendelea, anakutana na maneno yafuatayo:  
Utu ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa mizani na uwezo wa kutenda kama binadamu kwa viumbe au vitu visivyo na uwezo huo (Mlacha, 1989). Vitu kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama na ndege vinaonyeshwa kuwa vinafanya vitendo vya kibinadamu ingawa hawana uwezo wa kufanya hivyo. Kwa mfano, si ajabu katika fasihi kukuta ndege wakichumbiana, wakipendekeza ndoa, na hatimaye kuolewa na kuishi kwa furaha milele (Senkoro, 2006). Utumizi wa nafsi katika kazi za fasihi unakusudiwa kujenga dhamira kwa njia ya kufikirika ili msomaji aakisi kidogo ili kufahamu dhamira iliyokusudiwa ya mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi iliyo mbele yao. Katika riwaya ya *Kiu*, kuna matumizi ya unyambulishaji unaotumika kwa madhumuni haya, kama inavyoonyeshwa katika dondoo lifuatalo:
"Watu wanasema kwamba upendo haukutani kamwe, lakini kwa nini wako na Bahati?"
Bahati alilia kwa uchungu na huzuni, mpaka hata usingizi ukamtia huruma, upesi ukampitia na kumpumzisha kitandani. Aliamshwa na kelele za watu wanaokwenda msikitini, kwani alfajiri ilikuwa tayari imeingia. Hisia za muda za Bahati kila mara ziliongozwa na wapita njia. Alikuwa amezoea kusikia mienendo ya watu wanaokwenda kazini, shuleni, msikitini, ndege za abiria, na miito ya kusali (uk.20). Maneno yaliyosisitizwa katika kifungu hapo juu yanatumika kama mtu, kwa sababu katika maisha halisi ni mwanadamu tu anayeweza kuonyesha huruma kwa mtu mwingine au kiumbe. Usingizi ni hali ya mtu kupoteza fahamu, kama inavyoelezwa katika msemo wa Kiswahili usemao, "usingizi ni nusu ya kifo." Hata hivyo, katika kifungu kilicho hapo juu, usingizi unaonekana kuwa umepewa uwezo wa kuhisi huruma, kana kwamba ni binadamu. 5.1.5 Matumizi ya Mashaka katika Kiu

Mashaka ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za kifasihi kutayarisha kazi zao kwa namna ambayo hufikisha dhamira zao zilizokusudiwa kwa hadhira lengwa. Hii ni mbinu ya kumchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhu au ukweli wa jambo husika, na kuwafanya waendelee kusoma hadi pale watakapopata suluhu au maelezo fulani yatakayotoa jibu walilokusudia kupata (Senkoro, 2006). Mbinu ya mashaka hutumiwa kimakusudi na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi ili kumpa msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kuendelea kusoma, hasa pale kazi inayohusika inapokuwa ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji. Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa mfupi sana ikiwa kuna wakati wa mashaka ambao huvutia msomaji. Mashaka ni mbinu ya kifasihi ya kale ambayo hutumiwa sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, ametumia mbinu hii kwa jinsi anavyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake. Kwa mfano:

Jioni hiyo, alikuwa amejinyoosha kwenye kiti kilichokuwa ameegemea, macho yake yakiwa yameelekezwa kwenye dari, akihesabu dakika. Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kushindwa ulikuwa umemnyima furaha. Laiti kile alichotaka kingekuwa mikononi mwake, angekishika na kukata kiu yake. Ikiwa alichotaka kingeweza kununuliwa kwa pesa, bila shaka angekusanya kila senti aliyokuwa nayo. Lakini jambo lenyewe lilitegemea mapenzi ya mtu mwingine, mtu mwenye ladha na kiburi. Kwa hiyo hakuwa na chaguo ila kuuliza na kungoja (uk. 01–02). Kifungu hiki kina hali ya wasiwasi, kwani kuna jambo ambalo linamkosesha raha Mwinyi na kumtesa licha ya kuwa tajiri. Hili halijasemwa kwa uwazi, lakini inatajwa tu kwamba kama kupata kitu hicho kunahitajika pesa, Mwinyi angetoa.  
“Acha utani, Iddi,” Mwinyi alimkaripia. "Je, unafikiri mtoto kama huyo anaweza kumpenda mzee kama mimi (uk.05)?" Katika kifungu hiki, mvutano uliojengwa na mwandishi katika ukurasa wa kwanza wa riwaya yake unaanza kupata majibu katika ukurasa wa tano. Hapa ndipo linapotajwa suala linalomsumbua Mwinyi kiasi cha kukosa amani pamoja na utajiri wake mkubwa. Kitu hicho si kingine bali ni mapenzi aliyokuwa nayo kwa msichana aliyefahamika kwa jina la Bahati. Mwinyi alikuwa mtu wa miaka sitini na mbili, lakini alimpenda sana Bahati, ingawa alikuwa msichana mdogo ambaye alikuwa bado hajamaliza shule. Katika muktadha huu, mvutano mwingine unazuka: Je, Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa mpenzi wa mzee, kama alivyofanya Mwinyi? Hili pia linazua taharuki kwa wasomaji, ambao watalazimika kusoma zaidi ili kujua kitakachotokea kuhusiana na mapenzi ya Mwinyi kwa msichana mdogo Bahati. Matumizi ya mbinu hii ya mashaka yametumika kwa lengo la kuimarisha na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi katika riwaya ya Kiu. Mbinu hii inaonekana kutumika mara kwa mara, kwani kila jibu au suluhisho la mashaka ya awali linapopatikana, mashaka mengine huletwa (Mlacha, 1991). Kwa mfano, katika nukuu hiyo hapo juu tunapata suluhu kwamba kilichokuwa kikimsumbua Mwinyi Raha na kukosa usingizi ni mapenzi yake kwa bintiye Bahati. Baada ya kufahamu hilo, kumezuka wasiwasi mwingine iwapo msichana mdogo kama Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa na uhusiano na mzee Mwinyi ambaye anaweza kuwa babake Bahati. Wasomaji wataendelea kusoma hadi wapate suluhu, na baada ya hapo, watakumbana na wasiwasi mwingine. Hitimisho Lengo mahususi la kazi hii lilikuwa ni kuchanganua na kueleza mbinu za kimtindo zilizotumika kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya “Kiu” ya Mohamed Suleiman. Ipasavyo, matokeo hayo ni pamoja na matumizi ya mbinu za kimtindo kama vile herufi, misemo, mafumbo, utambulisho, na wasiwasi. Matokeo ya utafiti yanaonesha kuwa riwaya ya 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman ina mbinu nyingi za kimtindo, lakini katika utafiti huu tumezingatia tu matumizi ya mbinu ya uandishi wa herufi, misemo, sitiari, wasiwasi na mashaka. Sababu kuu ya kuteua mbinu hizi tano ni kwamba zinakidhi ipasavyo malengo ya utafiti huu. Utumiaji wa mbinu ya uandishi wa barua ulitumika kwa lengo la kuendeleza na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi, ambapo Bahati alitaka kujua iwapo Iddi anampenda kweli. Bahati alimuandikia barua Iddi kumjulisha kuwa sasa anampenda Mwinyi kwa dhati na kumtaka Iddi asimsumbue kwani sasa wanapanga harusi yao. Barua hii ilimtesa sana Iddi hata asijue la kufanya, maana tayari alishagundua kuwa mipango yote aliyopanga na Bahati sasa imeharibika. Hata hivyo, maudhui ya barua hiyo yalilenga kupima iwapo Iddi alimpenda Bahati kweli. Bahati alijua kuwa Iddi anampenda kwa sababu alikasirika baada ya kusoma barua aliyomtumia. Ilibainika kuwa Iddi hakukasirika kwa sababu alimpenda sana Bahati; bali aliona waziwazi Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kimtindo katika Riwaya za Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" Ali. Mipango ya Mwinyi ya kupata utajiri kupitia Bahati ilikuwa imegeuka kuwa ndoto isiyoweza kufikiwa. Mashaka ni mbinu nyingine ya kisanaa ambayo imetumiwa kuangazia dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman. Mbinu hii imetumika katika mpangilio wa njama na matukio, ambapo tangu mwanzo riwaya huanza na mashaka. Hali ya kuchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhu ya kile kinachoelezwa katika riwaya humjengea msomaji hamu ya kusoma zaidi, kwani atatamani kuendelea kusoma ili kufikia tamati ya tukio. Kwa mfano, mwanzoni mwa riwaya hii, inaelezwa kuwa Mwinyi anaishi kwa shida na hukosa furaha licha ya kuwa ni tajiri. Department of African Languages and Studies, Faculty of Languages, Sebha University, Libya
Keywords: Novel, Written Literature, Technical Techniques, Style, Literature

A B S T R A C T
A work of literature, including a novel, is formed by technique and content, which together constitute what we refer to as literature. Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and the use of language. These elements are utilized by writers in various ways depending on their skills and abilities.

5.1 Literary Techniques in the Swahili Novel  
5.1.1 The Use of the Letter Technique  
A letter is an ancient means of communication between an individual and another individual, an individual and a group, an institution and an individual, or between institutions. Its aim is to convey information or a particular message that is important for the intended recipient to know.  
Idi received the letter with surprise because he was not expecting it.
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1 Mbinu za Kifasihi katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili  
5.1.1 Matumizi ya Mbinu ya Barua  
Barua ni njia ya kale ya mawasiliano kati ya mtu binafsi na mtu mwingine, mtu binafsi na kikundi, taasisi na mtu binafsi, au kati ya taasisi. Lengo lake ni kuwasilisha taarifa au ujumbe fulani ambao ni muhimu kwa mlengwa kuufahamu.  
Idi aliipokea barua hiyo kwa mshangao kwa sababu hakuitarajia.

discourses.source_txt:
He turned the letter over and saw Bahati’s name written in hurried handwriting. He opened it and read:  
Idi,  
Don’t be surprised when I tell you that right now I am in bed with Mr. Mwinyi, and we are planning the day for our real wedding.
discourses.translated_txt:
Aligeuza barua na kuona jina la Bahati limeandikwa kwa mwandiko wa haraka haraka. Akaifungua na kusoma:  
Idi,  
Usishangae ninapokuambia kuwa sasa hivi niko kitandani kwa Mheshimiwa Mwinyi, na tunapanga siku ya harusi yetu halisi.

discourses.source_txt: It is not permitted to interfere with us because we have our own free will.

discourses.source_txt: The letter ignited a fire in Idi’s heart and boiled him with anger. It struck him like a sudden, fierce storm.

discourses.source_txt: Suddenly his eyes changed color, his forehead became furrowed, and his jaw dropped, in a display of intense anguish.

discourses.source_txt: He read that letter again, and the more he read it, the angrier he became.
discourses.translated_txt: Aliisoma tena barua hiyo, na kadiri alivyozidi kuisoma, ndivyo alivyozidi kuwa na hasira.

discourses.source_txt: This letter was written by Bahati to Idi, her lover whom she loves very much, but here she is informing him that she is now in love with another person named Mwinyi.
discourses.translated_txt: Barua hii iliandikwa na Bahati kwenda kwa Idi, mpenzi wake ambaye anampenda sana, lakini hapa anamtaarifu kuwa sasa yuko kwenye mapenzi na mtu mwingine anayeitwa Mwinyi.

discourses.source_txt: Mwinyi is Idi's boss, and Idi wanted Bahati to deceive Mwinyi by making him believe she loved him so that they could get money, while in reality, the one she truly loved was Idi. Now, it is truly shocking to see that the love between Mwinyi and Bahati has become genuine and not a joke as Idi had expected.

Sasa inashangaza sana kuona mapenzi kati ya Mwinyi na Bahati yamekuwa ya kweli na si mzaha kama Idi alivyotarajia.

discourses.source_txt: The theme of love, as well as that of theft and smuggling, are greatly developed through the use of the letter mentioned above.
discourses.translated_txt: Mandhari ya mapenzi, pamoja na ile ya wizi na magendo, yanaendelezwa sana kwa kutumia barua iliyotajwa hapo juu.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati is weighing whether Idi truly loves her, while Idi grows angry as his plan to gain Mwinyi's wealth through Bahati slips away.

discourses.source_txt: Also, through the above letter, the author develops the theme that not everything can turn out as one expects.
discourses.translated_txt: Pia, kupitia barua hiyo hapo juu, mwandishi huendeleza mada ambayo sio kila kitu kinaweza kutokea kama mtu anatarajia.

discourses.source_txt: Idi did not expect that telling Bahati to pretend to love Mwinyi so they could gain wealth would actually make Bahati truly fall in love with Mwinyi and leave him.
discourses.translated_txt: Idi hakutarajia kuwa kumwambia Bahati ajifanye anampenda Mwinyi ili wapate mali kwa kweli kungemfanya Bahati kumpenda sana Mwinyi na kumuacha.

5.1.2 The Use of Proverbs in Kiu

Proverbs are expressions that are similar to and resemble sayings used by human beings as tools of communication (Msokile, 1992).
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1.2 Matumizi ya Methali katika Kiu

Methali ni semi zinazofanana na kufanana na semi zinazotumiwa na binadamu kama nyenzo za mawasiliano (Msokile, 1992).

discourses.source_txt: However, proverbs often do not have two sides as is the case with sayings.
discourses.translated_txt: Walakini, methali mara nyingi hazina pande mbili kama ilivyo kwa misemo.

discourses.source_txt: A proverb, on its part, has two sides, where one side serves as a question and the other side provides the answer to the question posed (Wamitila, 2003).
discourses.translated_txt: Methali kwa upande wake ina pande mbili, ambapo upande mmoja hutumika kama swali na upande mwingine hutoa jibu la swali lililoulizwa (Wamitila, 2003).

discourses.source_txt: Proverbs are sayings that arise from expressions whose nature is that they emerge and disappear, and those that do not disappear but endure are what are called proverbs.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali ni misemo itokanayo na misemo ambayo asili yake ni kuibuka na kutoweka, na ile isiyotoweka bali huvumilia ndiyo inayoitwa methali.

discourses.source_txt: Proverbs are a literary technique used by authors of literary works to underscore or emphasize a particular theme they want their audience to grasp.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi ili kusisitiza au kusisitiza dhamira fulani wanayotaka hadhira yao ielewe.

discourses.source_txt: In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her.
discourses.translated_txt: Katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman ametumia methali katika kazi yake kama ifuatavyo: Mambo hayakuwa mazuri kwa Idi, kwani nia yake haikuwa kumpenda kikweli bali kumchezea tu.

discourses.source_txt: Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately.
discourses.translated_txt: Wazazi wengi wanaowajibika wanajua kuwa vijana wanapoingia kwenye mahusiano ya kimapenzi kabla ya ndoa mara nyingi huwapelekea kuchezeana na suala la ndoa kupotea. Kwa hiyo, akiwa mzazi, Cheusi alimtaka bintiye kumalizana na Idi mara moja.

discourses.source_txt: The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali iliyotumika katika kifungu hapo juu imetumika kujenga na kusisitiza mada ya mwongozo wa mama kwa mtoto wake.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mazoea ni kitu ambacho hutengeneza tabia, na mazoea daima yanaendelea (Ritzer, 2008).

discourses.source_txt: If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged.
discourses.translated_txt: Iwapo katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wataachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa, wataichukulia kuwa inakubalika, na suala la kuoana halitakuwa na umuhimu wowote kwao. Wazazi watimize wajibu wao ipasavyo ili wanajamii hasa vijana waone kuwa mahusiano kabla ya ndoa ni jambo baya ambalo halipaswi kuhimizwa kamwe.

discourses.source_txt:
5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences.
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1.3 Matumizi ya Sitiari katika Kiu

Tamathali ya semi ni tamathali ya semi ambayo hutumiwa kulinganisha vitu viwili vyenye sifa tofauti bila kutumia viunganishi vya ulinganishi, kama ilivyo kwa tashibiha (Kyando, 2013). Vitu vinavyolinganishwa vinachukuliwa kuwa sawa kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote.

discourses.source_txt: For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza kusema, "Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo aliyejificha kwenye mti." Hapa Mwajuma anafananishwa na sungura kana kwamba ni vitu viwili vinavyofanana kabisa bila tofauti yoyote.

discourses.source_txt: The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader.
discourses.translated_txt: Madhumuni makuu ya kutumia mafumbo katika kazi za fasihi ni kusisitiza dhamira inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji.

discourses.source_txt:
Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing.
discourses.translated_txt:
Mohamed Suleiman alitumia sitiari aliposema:  
Watu waliposema hakuna aliyewahi kumzidi ujanja Mwinyi, maneno yao hayakuwa ya kutia chumvi. Mwinyi alikuwa na pesa za kutosha kujinunulia vitu vingi ambavyo mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angeweza kutamani, isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu.

discourses.source_txt: That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01).
discourses.translated_txt: Hilo ndilo lililomfanya ahisi kana kwamba maisha yake yote yamepotea, na kwamba utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki ya wali iliyoharibiwa na mchanga (uk.01).

discourses.source_txt: The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno yaliyosisitizwa kwa wino katika msemo hapa yanaeleza msemo kwamba kitu kizuri sasa kimegeuka kuwa kibaya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu, na kitu cha thamani sasa kimepoteza thamani yake.

discourses.source_txt: Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him.
discourses.translated_txt: Bwana Mwinyi alikuwa ni tajiri mwenye kila aina ya utajiri, lakini alitamani sana kuwa na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na mwanadada Bahati ambaye alikuwa akimpenda sana. Kila mbinu aliyoijaribu ilishindikana kumshinda Bahati, hali iliyopelekea kulalamika kuwa “utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki iliyochanganywa na mchanga,” akimaanisha utajiri wake haukumsaidia chochote na wala haukuwa na faida yoyote kwake.

discourses.source_txt: Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand.
discourses.translated_txt: Kimsingi, keki ya wali iliyochanganywa na mchanga huwa haiwezi kuliwa na kupoteza ladha yake yote kwa sababu mlaji anaogopa meno yake yatauma kwenye mchanga.

discourses.source_txt: This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person.
discourses.translated_txt: Msemo huu kwa hakika umetumika kutilia mkazo mada ya mapenzi—kwamba ikiwa mtu ni tajiri katika kila maana ya kimaada lakini akakosa upendo anaoutamani, basi utajiri wake unakuwa hauna maana na kuwafanya waishi kwa dhiki na uchungu wa akili kuliko hata maskini.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanasosholojia wanakiri kwamba kuna vitu fulani ambavyo kwa ujumla huchukuliwa kuwa vya kutamanika sana kuwa navyo, kama vile utajiri (Cross, 2011).

discourses.source_txt: However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything.
discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, inafika wakati mtu anakosa kitu ambacho alidhani ni kidogo, na mali yake haimsaidii kukipata, ingawa aliamini kuwa utajiri wake ndio ufunguo wa kupata kila kitu.

discourses.source_txt: This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love.
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni sawa na kusema kwamba keki ya wali sasa ina mchanga ndani yake, kwa kuwa utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haungeweza kumwezesha kushinda penzi la Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi mengine ya msemo huo yanaonekana wakati Cheusi, ambaye ni mamake Bahati, alipokuwa akimwonya bintiye kuhusu uhusiano wake na Idi.

discourses.source_txt:
He says:
There was a brief but bitter silence.
discourses.translated_txt:
Anasema:
Kukawa kimya kifupi lakini kichungu.

discourses.source_txt: Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing.
discourses.translated_txt: Kisha Cheusi akaendelea kumshauri: “Huyo Idi wako hebu niambie hakutaki hana lolote.

discourses.source_txt: Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you.
discourses.translated_txt: Yeyote anayetamani mwanamke kweli amuoe. Anataka tu kukuchezea kisha akutupe, akiendelea huku anakucheka.

discourses.source_txt:
I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart.
discourses.translated_txt:
Tayari nimegundua kwamba kwa sababu tu umesoma Kiingereza chako unafikiri mimi sijui, basi ... Siku moja utalia kama mbwa, utainua mdomo, na nitakuwa hapa (uk. 25–26).” Katika kifungu hiki mwandishi anatumia msemo, “utalia kama mbwa, mdomo utainuliwa,” kurejelea mada ya mwongozo na maonyo yanayotolewa na mama kwa mtoto wake. Cheusi alikuwa akimwonya bintiye Bahati kuhusu uhusiano aliokuwa ameanza nao
Muda huo Iddi dereva wake aliingia bila kubisha hodi. Mwinyi alishtuka na kumuuliza, “Mbona umechelewa?” Iddi alijifuta jasho kuonesha juhudi aliyoifanya, akatikisa kichwa kwa huzuni na kusema, “Nimekuta mlango umefungwa.” Maneno hayo yalivunja moyo wa Mwinyi.

discourses.source_txt: He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him.
discourses.translated_txt: Aliinama mabega yake na kujikunyata kwenye kiti, akihisi maisha hayakuwa ya haki kwake.

discourses.source_txt: Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come.
discourses.translated_txt: Kungoja bila mwisho—miezi sita ilikuwa imepita, na hamu isiyokoma ililemea sana. Alikuwa tayari amevumilia vya kutosha; lakini bado hakujua siku ya msaada ingefika lini.

discourses.source_txt: But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02).
discourses.translated_txt: Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: "Chochote kinachokuja kwa njia yako, kikubali" (uk. 02).

discourses.source_txt: The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya sitiari katika kishazi hapo juu yanaonyesha kuwa maneno hulinganishwa na kisu au kitu chochote chenye ncha kali chenye uwezo wa kukata kitu.

discourses.source_txt: “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked.
discourses.translated_txt: "Maneno yale yalimpiga Mwinyi sana," ni kauli inayoonyesha matumaini ya Mwinyi kumshinda Bahati yalitoweka mara tu alipopata taarifa kutoka kwa Idi kwamba hakumpata Bahati na kwamba mlango wa Bahati ulikuwa umefungwa.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kwamba mtu anaweza kufikia mahali ambapo anapoteza matumaini ya kupata kitu ambacho amekuwa akitamani kwa muda mrefu lakini hawezi kukipata (Webster, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape.
discourses.translated_txt: Kupoteza tumaini maishani ni jambo baya kwa sababu kunaweza kumfanya mtu afanye jambo baya ambalo linaweza hata kuhatarisha wengine. Kwa mfano, kukata tamaa kwa Mwinyi kwa kukosa kuwa na Bahati kunaweza kumfanya achukue uamuzi wa kufanya uhalifu kama vile ubakaji.

discourses.source_txt: The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya kwa mwathiriwa lakini pia kwa mhusika, kwani kinaweza kusababisha kukaa jela maisha yake yote.

discourses.source_txt: For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mzee wa miaka sitini na mbili kama Mwinyi kufungwa ni jambo baya sana ambalo linaweza kumfanya afie gerezani.

discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, inasemekana kwamba suala hilo kwa kweli lilikuwa tabia ya mtu—na mtu huyo ni mwenye kiburi na majivuno.

discourses.source_txt: These descriptions show that the thing in question is not specified, which makes the keen reader want to find out what exactly it is that is troubling Mwinyi so much. The use of suspense will compel the reader to continue reading the novel 'Kiu' until they discover what it is that is bothering Mwinyi.
discourses.translated_txt: Maelezo haya yanaonesha kuwa jambo husika halijaainishwa, jambo linalomfanya msomaji makini kutaka kujua ni nini hasa kinachomsumbua sana Mwinyi. Matumizi ya mashaka yatamlazimisha msomaji kuendelea kusoma riwaya ya 'Kiu' hadi agundue ni kitu gani kinamsumbua Mwinyi.

discourses.source_txt:
As the reader continues, they come across the following words:  
Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989).
discourses.translated_txt:
Wakati msomaji anaendelea, anakutana na maneno yafuatayo:  
Utu ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa mizani na uwezo wa kutenda kama binadamu kwa viumbe au vitu visivyo na uwezo huo (Mlacha, 1989).

discourses.source_txt: Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Vitu kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama na ndege vinaonyeshwa kuwa vinafanya vitendo vya kibinadamu ingawa hawana uwezo wa kufanya hivyo. Kwa mfano, si ajabu katika fasihi kukuta ndege wakichumbiana, wakipendekeza ndoa, na hatimaye kuolewa na kuishi kwa furaha milele (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them.
discourses.translated_txt: Utumizi wa nafsi katika kazi za fasihi unakusudiwa kujenga dhamira kwa njia ya kufikirika ili msomaji aakisi kidogo ili kufahamu dhamira iliyokusudiwa ya mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi iliyo mbele yao.

discourses.source_txt:
In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed.
discourses.translated_txt:
Katika riwaya ya *Kiu*, kuna matumizi ya unyambulishaji unaotumika kwa madhumuni haya, kama inavyoonyeshwa katika dondoo lifuatalo:
"Watu wanasema kwamba upendo haukutani kamwe, lakini kwa nini wako na Bahati?"
Bahati alilia kwa uchungu na huzuni, mpaka hata usingizi ukamtia huruma, upesi ukampitia na kumpumzisha kitandani.

discourses.source_txt: She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken.
discourses.translated_txt: Aliamshwa na kelele za watu wanaokwenda msikitini, kwani alfajiri ilikuwa tayari imeingia.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20).
discourses.translated_txt: Hisia za muda za Bahati kila mara ziliongozwa na wapita njia. Alikuwa amezoea kusikia mienendo ya watu wanaokwenda kazini, shuleni, msikitini, ndege za abiria, na miito ya kusali (uk.20).

discourses.source_txt: The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno yaliyosisitizwa katika kifungu hapo juu yanatumika kama mtu, kwa sababu katika maisha halisi ni mwanadamu tu anayeweza kuonyesha huruma kwa mtu mwingine au kiumbe. Usingizi ni hali ya mtu kupoteza fahamu, kama inavyoelezwa katika msemo wa Kiswahili usemao, "usingizi ni nusu ya kifo." Hata hivyo, katika kifungu kilicho hapo juu, usingizi unaonekana kuwa umepewa uwezo wa kuhisi huruma, kana kwamba ni binadamu.

discourses.source_txt:
5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience.
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1.5 Matumizi ya Mashaka katika Kiu

Mashaka ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za kifasihi kutayarisha kazi zao kwa namna ambayo hufikisha dhamira zao zilizokusudiwa kwa hadhira lengwa.

discourses.source_txt: This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni mbinu ya kumchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhu au ukweli wa jambo husika, na kuwafanya waendelee kusoma hadi pale watakapopata suluhu au maelezo fulani yatakayotoa jibu walilokusudia kupata (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader.
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu ya mashaka hutumiwa kimakusudi na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi ili kumpa msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kuendelea kusoma, hasa pale kazi inayohusika inapokuwa ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji. Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa mfupi sana ikiwa kuna wakati wa mashaka ambao huvutia msomaji.

discourses.source_txt:
Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst.
discourses.translated_txt:
Mashaka ni mbinu ya kifasihi ya kale ambayo hutumiwa sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, ametumia mbinu hii kwa jinsi anavyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake. Kwa mfano:

Jioni hiyo, alikuwa amejinyoosha kwenye kiti kilichokuwa ameegemea, macho yake yakiwa yameelekezwa kwenye dari, akihesabu dakika. Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kushindwa ulikuwa umemnyima furaha. Laiti kile alichotaka kingekuwa mikononi mwake, angekishika na kukata kiu yake.

discourses.source_txt: If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had.
discourses.translated_txt: Ikiwa alichotaka kingeweza kununuliwa kwa pesa, bila shaka angekusanya kila senti aliyokuwa nayo.

discourses.source_txt: But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride.
discourses.translated_txt: Lakini jambo lenyewe lilitegemea mapenzi ya mtu mwingine, mtu mwenye ladha na kiburi.

discourses.source_txt: So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02).
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa hiyo hakuwa na chaguo ila kuuliza na kungoja (uk. 01–02).

discourses.source_txt: This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy.
discourses.translated_txt: Kifungu hiki kina hali ya wasiwasi, kwani kuna jambo ambalo linamkosesha raha Mwinyi na kumtesa licha ya kuwa tajiri.

discourses.source_txt:
This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him.
discourses.translated_txt:
Hili halijasemwa kwa uwazi, lakini inatajwa tu kwamba kama kupata kitu hicho kunahitajika pesa, Mwinyi angetoa.  
“Acha utani, Iddi,” Mwinyi alimkaripia.

discourses.source_txt: “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five.
discourses.translated_txt: "Je, unafikiri mtoto kama huyo anaweza kumpenda mzee kama mimi (uk.05)?" Katika kifungu hiki, mvutano uliojengwa na mwandishi katika ukurasa wa kwanza wa riwaya yake unaanza kupata majibu katika ukurasa wa tano.

discourses.source_txt: This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth.
discourses.translated_txt: Hapa ndipo linapotajwa suala linalomsumbua Mwinyi kiasi cha kukosa amani pamoja na utajiri wake mkubwa.

discourses.source_txt: That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitu hicho si kingine bali ni mapenzi aliyokuwa nayo kwa msichana aliyefahamika kwa jina la Bahati. Mwinyi alikuwa mtu wa miaka sitini na mbili, lakini alimpenda sana Bahati, ingawa alikuwa msichana mdogo ambaye alikuwa bado hajamaliza shule.

discourses.source_txt: In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: Katika muktadha huu, mvutano mwingine unazuka: Je, Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa mpenzi wa mzee, kama alivyofanya Mwinyi? Hili pia linazua taharuki kwa wasomaji, ambao watalazimika kusoma zaidi ili kujua kitakachotokea kuhusiana na mapenzi ya Mwinyi kwa msichana mdogo Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya mbinu hii ya mashaka yametumika kwa lengo la kuimarisha na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi katika riwaya ya Kiu.

discourses.source_txt: This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991).
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu hii inaonekana kutumika mara kwa mara, kwani kila jibu au suluhisho la mashaka ya awali linapopatikana, mashaka mengine huletwa (Mlacha, 1991).

discourses.source_txt: For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano, katika nukuu hiyo hapo juu tunapata suluhu kwamba kilichokuwa kikimsumbua Mwinyi Raha na kukosa usingizi ni mapenzi yake kwa bintiye Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father.
discourses.translated_txt: Baada ya kufahamu hilo, kumezuka wasiwasi mwingine iwapo msichana mdogo kama Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa na uhusiano na mzee Mwinyi ambaye anaweza kuwa babake Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety.
discourses.translated_txt: Wasomaji wataendelea kusoma hadi wapate suluhu, na baada ya hapo, watakumbana na wasiwasi mwingine.

discourses.source_txt: Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety.
discourses.translated_txt: Hitimisho Lengo mahususi la kazi hii lilikuwa ni kuchanganua na kueleza mbinu za kimtindo zilizotumika kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya “Kiu” ya Mohamed Suleiman. Ipasavyo, matokeo hayo ni pamoja na matumizi ya mbinu za kimtindo kama vile herufi, misemo, mafumbo, utambulisho, na wasiwasi.

discourses.source_txt: The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research.
discourses.translated_txt: Matokeo ya utafiti yanaonesha kuwa riwaya ya 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman ina mbinu nyingi za kimtindo, lakini katika utafiti huu tumezingatia tu matumizi ya mbinu ya uandishi wa herufi, misemo, sitiari, wasiwasi na mashaka. Sababu kuu ya kuteua mbinu hizi tano ni kwamba zinakidhi ipasavyo malengo ya utafiti huu.

discourses.source_txt: The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: Utumiaji wa mbinu ya uandishi wa barua ulitumika kwa lengo la kuendeleza na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi, ambapo Bahati alitaka kujua iwapo Iddi anampenda kweli. Bahati alimuandikia barua Iddi kumjulisha kuwa sasa anampenda Mwinyi kwa dhati na kumtaka Iddi asimsumbue kwani sasa wanapanga harusi yao. Barua hii ilimtesa sana Iddi hata asijue la kufanya, maana tayari alishagundua kuwa mipango yote aliyopanga na Bahati sasa imeharibika. Hata hivyo, maudhui ya barua hiyo yalilenga kupima iwapo Iddi alimpenda Bahati kweli.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him.
discourses.translated_txt: Bahati alijua kuwa Iddi anampenda kwa sababu alikasirika baada ya kusoma barua aliyomtumia.

discourses.source_txt: It turned out that Iddi was not upset because he really loved Bahati; rather, he saw clearly
discourses.translated_txt: Ilibainika kuwa Iddi hakukasirika kwa sababu alimpenda sana Bahati; bali aliona waziwazi

discourses.translated_txt: Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kimtindo katika Riwaya za Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" Ali.

discourses.source_txt: Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream.
discourses.translated_txt: Mipango ya Mwinyi ya kupata utajiri kupitia Bahati ilikuwa imegeuka kuwa ndoto isiyoweza kufikiwa.

discourses.source_txt: Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense.
discourses.translated_txt: Mashaka ni mbinu nyingine ya kisanaa ambayo imetumiwa kuangazia dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman. Mbinu hii imetumika katika mpangilio wa njama na matukio, ambapo tangu mwanzo riwaya huanza na mashaka.

discourses.source_txt: The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person.
discourses.translated_txt: Hali ya kuchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhu ya kile kinachoelezwa katika riwaya humjengea msomaji hamu ya kusoma zaidi, kwani atatamani kuendelea kusoma ili kufikia tamati ya tukio. Kwa mfano, mwanzoni mwa riwaya hii, inaelezwa kuwa Mwinyi anaishi kwa shida na hukosa furaha licha ya kuwa ni tajiri.

discourses.source_txt: The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitu kinachotajwa kumnyima furaha Mwinyi ni mapenzi yake kwa Bahati, jambo ambalo anaamini haliwezi kufanikiwa kwa kuwa yeye ni mzee na Bahati ni mwanamke mdogo.

discourses.source_txt: Other stylistic techniques used to develop social themes in the novel "Kiu" include proverbs, metaphors, and personification. These literary techniques have been employed to emphasize various issues related to social themes in the novel "Kiu."
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu nyinginezo za kimtindo zinazotumika kukuza dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya "Kiu" ni pamoja na methali, tamathali za semi na tamathali za usemi. Mbinu hizi za kifasihi zimetumika ili kusisitiza masuala mbalimbali yanayohusiana na dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya "Kiu."
